title: Round 9 - the stability rule, pre-registered and applied
focus: Round 8's momentum-seat override asked for its own reasoning to become a rule. Round 9 is that rule: a stability gate requiring a card's worst rank across three historical matrices to be no worse than fifth, pre-registered before this round's own numbers existed.
headline: The pre-registered stability rule filled only one of four ranked seats - B-momentum won the momentum seat outright with no override needed - but every other candidate failed the new gate, so the desk owner chose to keep round 8's five-card roster running while the gate was repaired for round 10.
outcome:
Gate A (positive median annualized adjusted excess at the 5-year and 10-year rungs against both benchmarks) again passed the same eight cards prior rounds found. Gate L was tightened to also require recent activity, closing a hole where c07-chop had cleared round 8's liveness bar on three trades and then sat at 100% cash for 92 sessions. The new Gate S required a worst rank across three historical matrices no worse than fifth of fifteen.

Only three cards cleared all three gates - B-momentum, B4-tight-stop and B3-concentrated - and all three are the same base family, so distinctness allowed exactly one seat. B-momentum won the ranking outright among the three, so the momentum seat fell out of the rule rather than a person's judgement, and no override was recorded because none was needed.

But no other discipline or family produced a single survivor of all three gates: A-rotation, B2-hold-90, C-trend and H-trend-diversified each cleared Gates A and L and failed Gate S. A-rotation's failure was the sharpest case, since it has no round-4 matrix result at all, having been retired after round 4 and reinstated only for round 5 - an availability gap that Gate S treated identically to a bad rank rather than inventing a favorable number.

Given a two-card output (B-momentum plus the unranked ladder-qld-schd), the desk owner was offered a choice: ship the thin roster, or keep round 8's five-card roster running while Gate S was repaired. The second was chosen. Two structural defects in Gate S were diagnosed as the reason a simple re-threshold would not have been enough: it selects against distinctness (a global top-five bar can only be cleared by the strongest family, which distinctness then collapses to one seat), and it re-measures competitiveness that Gate A and the ranking already test, rather than the dispersion property the round-8 override was actually reaching for.
owner_override: The pre-registered rule produced only a two-card roster (B-momentum plus the unranked ladder-qld-schd); rather than ship that, the desk owner chose to keep round 8's five-card roster (B-momentum, A-rotation, c07-chop, H-trend-diversified, ladder-qld-schd) running unchanged and have Gate S repaired for round 10.
carries_forward: Gate S needs repairing, not just re-thresholding: replace its global level bar with a coverage clause (a result on at least 2 of 3 matrices, never imputed) and a pure dispersion bar (max rank minus min rank), and make the seat count an output rather than a fixed target of four.
A-rotation's Gate S failure is a data-availability artifact from an absent round-4 matrix, not a performance failure, and is worth a considered decision either way in the repaired gate.
Fix 4 (scoring the live desk's own matrix, weighted above backtests) is closer still and remains the standing recommendation, repeated across every round since round 6.
The benchmark anchor should be stated wherever a SPY figure crosses a round boundary, still costing attention each time it is skipped.
